This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH5 2.

The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 02.10.2022 at about 4.05 a.m. he had been travelling in a car bearing Reg.No.KA41MD5855 on DoddamannuguddeVaddaradoddi Village,
New National Highway, Ramanagara, a Ashok Leyland Tusker Super vehocle bearing Reg.No.KA 01C4844 came in high speed rash and negligently and dashed against their car, due to the said accident, he has sustained grievous injuries, hence immediately he was taken to Ramanagara Government Hospital, after first aid, he was shifted to H.K.Hospital Kengeri, for which he has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/ towards medicines, treatment, food, nourishing and travelling expenses.
3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 44 years, hale and healthy, working as agriculturist and also doing dairy farming, thereby earning SCCH5 Rs.25,000/ p.m.,
due to this accident he is unable to work, suffering from severe pain and mental agony, he has lost his income and earning capacity.

Out of this accident crime No.113/2022 is registered against the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA01C4844 before the Ramanagara Traffic police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
R1 is the owner, R2 is insurer of the said lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.20,00,000/.
4.

On service of notice, R1/owner has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner, he is the R.C.Owner of the Ashok Leyland Tusker super lorry bearing Reg.No.KA01 C4844 and said vehicle is insured with R2, the policy was valid as on the date of accident.
Further driver of the said lorry had SCCH5 valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. R2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner, he is the insurer of the Goods Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA01C 4844 and his liability to pay the compensation is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

He is entitled to take shelter under Venkatesh.H vs N. Nagendra on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140277140/
2 Sec.147 and 150(2) of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further submitted that, alleged accident is took place on 02.10.2022 and complaint is lodged on 03.10.2022,
so that, there is delay of one day in lodging the complaint.

The driver of the offending goods vehicle does not possess valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident and the said vehicle does not possess valid permit to ply in the place of accident.

Further submitted SCCH5 that,
petition is liable to be dismissed for nonjoinder of necessary party i.e., owner and insurer of the car bearing Reg.No.KA41MD5855.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 02.10.2022 at about 4.05 a.m. when petitioner was travelling in a car bearing Reg.No.KA41MD5855, near middle of Doddamannugudde Vaddaradoddi Village, new NH, Ramanagara, at that time, one Ashok Leyland Tusker Super bearing Reg.No.KA01C4844 driven by its rider in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the petitioner car and SCCH5 caused accident,
as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
7.
In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW1, examined 1 witness as PW2 and marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, driver of the lorry is examined as RW1 and closed his evidence.
8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

The counsel for R2 has relied on a decision reported in (2018) 6 Supreme Court Cases 765 in between Nishan Singh and Others V/s. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and 2005 ACJ 1323 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s.
Prembai Patel SCCH5 and Others.

Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1: In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW1, in his chief examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is Venkatesh.H vs N. Nagendra on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140277140/

copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.7.
SCCH5 10.
In crossexamination admits that, their car dashed on hind portion of the lorry, further admits that, lorry was loaded with beer bottles.

Further admits that, very accident is occurred on highway road, further deposed hat, his sister's husband Balakrishna had been running their car, further they were seen the lorry at the distance of 60 feet, further admits that, they know that, they shall maintain minimum distance to avoid the accident.
11.
Further deposed that, Balakrishna had driving licence, copy of the said driving licence is not furnished.
Further in crossexamination deposed that, lorry was in 90 km. speed and their car was moving in 70 - 80 km. speed, further deposed that, lorry is not turtled down.
12. On the other hand, driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA01C4844 is examined as RW1.
In his chief SCCH5 examination deposed that, very accident is occurred in National Highway in middle of the road while moving with beer loaded lorry.

Further deposed that, car bearing Reg.No.KA41MD5855 came in high speed and dashed against hind portion of the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA01C 4844, so that, his lorry is damaged on hind portion, car is damaged on front portion.
Very accident is occurred due to negligency of the car driver.

In crossexamination admits that, he has not lodged the complaint, further admits that, he has admitted the guilt before the court and paid PF.
13.
The police papers marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.7 speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the lorry driver.
Ex.P.4 hand sketch map speaks that, very accident is occurred in middle of the road.

As per say of the petitioner in his petition and chief SCCH5 examination, lorry came in high speed and dashed against his car, but in crossexamination admits that, car is dashed on hind portion of the lorry.
IMV report marked at Ex.P.6 also speaks that, car is damaged on front portion and lorry is damaged on back portion.
Further as per case of the PW1 and RW1 lorry was loaded with beer bottles, both the vehicles are moving on same route towards same direction.
14. As per say of the PW1, lorry was in 90 km. speed and his car was in 70 - 80 km. speed.
Further as per say of the PW1, lorry was moving and which was not far anywhere.

Under such circumstances, it goes to show that, with regard to the speed PW1 has deposed his false evidence,
because if lorry is in high speed and car was in low speed, it is not possible to imagine the accident.

Further as per case of the petitioner, lorry came in high SCCH5 speed and dashed against his car,
but in cross examination himself admitted that, car is dashed on hind portion of the lorry.
IMV report supports the version of the RW1/lorry driver, however charge sheet is against the lorry driver.

sentences.text: The finding so recorded by the tribunal has been affirmed by the High Court, by observing that the evidence was clearly indicative of the fact that the Maruti Car was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, which was the cause for SCCH5 accident of this nature and resulting in death of one of the passengers in the Maruti Car.
The Maruti car was driven by none other than PW2 Manjeet Singh.

In his evidence, he has admitted that the subject truck was running ahead of the Maruti Car for quite some time about one kilometre and at the time of accident, the distance between the truck and Maruti car was only 1015 ft.
He has also admitted that the law mandates maintaining sufficient distance between two vehicles running in the same direction.
It is also not in dispute that the road on which the two vehicles were moving was only about 14 feet wide.

It is unfathomable that on such a narrow road,
the subject truck would move at a high speed as alleged.

In any case the Maruti car which was following the truck was expected to maintain a safe distance, as envisaged in Regulation 23 of the Rules of the Road Regulations, 1989 which reads thus;
SCCH5 "23. Distance from vehicles in front - The driver of a motor vehicle moving behind another vehicle shall keep at a sufficient distance from that other vehicle to avoid collision if the vehicle in front should suddenly slow down or stop".
The expression "sufficient distance" has not been defined in the Regulations or elsewhere.
The thumb rule of sufficient distance is atleast a safe distance of two to three seconds gap in ideal conditions to avert collision and to allow the following driver time to respond.
The distance of 1015 ft.between the truck and Maruti car was certainly not a safe distance for which the driver of the Maruti car must take the blame.
It must necessarily follow that the finding on the issue under consideration ought to be against the claimants.
13. The tribunal also noted that there was no evidence on record to indicate that the driver of the truck suddenly applied his brake in the middle of the road.
Further, the findings on Issue 1 recorded SCCH5 by the tribunal is that there was no evidence regarding exact place of occurrence of accident and having taken survey.

Therefore, the issue under consideration was answered against the appellant claimants, namely, that the subject truck was not driven rashly and negligently by the truck driver nor had he brought the truck in the centre of the road at the right side or applied sudden brake as being the cause of the accident.
Being a concurrent finding of fact and a possible view, needs no interference".
On going through the above cited citation it is noticed that, Maruthi car dashed against the lorry on its hind portion.
Further inmate of the said car is died.

In this regard Hon'ble Supreme Court of India observed that, Maruthi car driver has not maintained the sufficient distance and accident is occurred due to his own negligency and there is no negligency of the truck driver.

In the case on hand also, there is no evidence on record except the charge sheet to show that,
truck driver has taken the lorry on right side without giving signals.
Further evidence of the petitioner is contradict to his pleadings with regard to speed of his car and lorry.
Considering the same, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, there is contributory negligence of the truck driver and car driver.

Under such circumstances, it was duty of the petitioner to bring the owner and insurer of the car bearing Reg.No.KA41MD5855 in this case as respondents, but knowingly he has not made them as parties to the proceedings, under such circumstances, respondent No.1 and 2 are not responsible for the same, said fact is proved by the R2 that, petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties, because there is contributory negligence of the car driver, so that, owner SCCH5 and insurer of the said car are necessary parties to this petition.
Further there is no dispute about the place, date and time of the accident.

Hence considering the same, negligency of the car driver is considered at the rate of 50%, which is borne by the petitioner himself as he has not made owner and insurer of the car as parties to this petition and negligency of the driver of the Ashok Layland Tusker super vehicle is considered at the rate of 50%.
Considering the same, I have answered above Issue No.1 partly in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained comminuted fracture dislocation of the right shoulder, for which he underwent ORIF with ethibond sutures and CC screws.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.4, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued SCCH5 by H.K.Hospital, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 02.10.2022 to 03.10.2022.
18.

Insupport of his case, Dr.Nagaraj B.N. Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS is examined as PW2 and furnished clinical notes marked as Ex.P.12 and Xray Films marked as Ex.P.13 and he has assessed total disability of the right arm at the rate of 33% and whole body physical disability at the rate of 11%.
19.

In crossexamination, admits that he is not a treated Doctor, fracture is united, he has not taken opinion from treated Doctor, he has assessed only physical disability, regular usage of limb will improve the muscle power, further denied that, in view of union of the fracture there will be no disability.
20. The wound certificate marked at Ex.P.5 speaks that, he sustained grievous injuries in right hand in this SCCH5 accident.
Ex.P.8 discharge summary speaks that, there is open reduction and internal fixation with screws medical bills is also on record.
Petitioner is aged about 44 years, as per say of the petitioner, he is agriculturist, considering the same, functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 10%.

21. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 44 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.11, wherein it is clearly mentioned year of birth of the petitioner as 1975, the alleged accident is occurred in the year 2022, accordingly relying on Ex.P.11 his age is considered about 47 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 13 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

Keeping in mind injuries caused to the petitioner, treatment taken, expenses incurred and also the pain suffered, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to allot compensation under other heads, accordingly for pain and sufferings compensation of Rs.15,000/

Further driver of the lorry had valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident, in this regard there is no dispute by the respondents.
27. As discussed in issue No.1, considering contributory negligence by both the parties, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, 50% of the award amount i.e., Rs.2,13,187/ (50% of Rs.4,26,373/)
shall be paid by R2 along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of petition till realization of entire amount.
Remaining 50% of the amount i.e., Rs.2,13,186/ (50% of Rs.4,26,373/) shall be borne by the petitioner for non inclusion of the owner and insurer SCCH5 of the car bearing Reg.No.KA41MD5855.
Accordingly, I have answered Issue No.3 partly in affirmative.

28. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,13,187/ (Rupees Two Lakhs Thirteen Thousand One Hundred Eighty Seven Only) i.e., 50% of Rs.4,26,373/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization which shall be paid by respondent No.2 along with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

Remaining 50% compensation of Rs.2,13,186/ i.e., 50% of Rs.4,26,373/
shall be borne by the petitioner.

SCCH5 The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
